netanya-bagrut-record-2026.title: Matriculation eligibility rate in Netanya reaches 87.5%, the city's highest in a decade
netanya-bagrut-record-2026.dek: According to Education Ministry data for the 2024-25 school year, the city's eligibility rate rose by 2.7 percentage points in one year and clearly passed the national average.
body: The share of students eligible for a bagrut (Israeli matriculation certificate) in Netanya stood at 87.5% in the 2024-25 school year (Hebrew year 5785). The data come from the Education Ministry's “Educational Picture” report, which was published this week and presented by the Netanya Municipality. According to the municipality, this is the highest rate recorded in the city in the past decade.

In the previous year, 2023-24, the city's eligibility rate was 84.8%. In 2015 it was only 67.6%, so within a decade there was a rise of almost 20 percentage points. The national average in 2024-25 was 77.9%, and Netanya is 9.6 percentage points above it.

In English, too, the city is above the average. At the 5-unit level (the highest level), the rate in Netanya was 51.6%, compared with 48.7% nationwide, and at the 4-unit level it was 23.3%, compared with 18.5%. In mathematics the picture is mixed: at the 4-unit level the city is above the average, with 25.1% compared with 22.9%, but at the 5-unit level it is slightly below, with 16.3% compared with 17.1%.

The municipality noted that the overall figure also includes new immigrants who take their exams in Hebrew shortly after arriving, special education students, and some of the ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) students who do not sit for the bagrut exams.

Mayor Avi Salama praised the education staff and said the achievement reflects shared professional work, and promised to keep investing in the system. At the municipality's Education and Society Administration, the rise was attributed to tutoring programs, close tracking of students' progress, personalized support and expanded options for completing the exams.
keyPoints: 87.5% bagrut eligibility in Netanya in 2024-25, compared with 84.8% a year earlier
The national average was 77.9%
In 5-unit mathematics the city is slightly below the national average
netanya-bagrut-record-2026.whatItMeans: More students in Netanya finish high school with a full bagrut certificate, but there is still room for improvement in high-level mathematics.
faq: What was the bagrut eligibility rate in Netanya last year?
In the 2023-24 school year the rate was 84.8%.
In which subject is Netanya below the national average?
In 5-unit mathematics: 16.3% in the city compared with 17.1% nationwide.

maccabi-netanya-beat-kiryat-shmona.title: Maccabi Netanya beat Ironi Kiryat Shmona 1-0 and ended a run of four games without a win
maccabi-netanya-beat-kiryat-shmona.dek: A second-half penalty gave Roni Levy's team three points, its first clean sheet since the opening round, and a move up to sixth place.
body: Maccabi Netanya beat Ironi Kiryat Shmona 1-0 on Saturday evening in the Israeli Premier League (Ligat Ha'al). The first half ended with no goals, and the only goal was scored around the 74th minute, from a penalty kick taken from 11 meters by Matheus Dabo, after a handball in the box by a Kiryat Shmona player. On the touchlines were Roni Levy for Netanya and Shai Brada for Kiryat Shmona.

The win ended a run of four games without a victory for Netanya. Thanks to it, the team moved up to sixth place in the table, at least temporarily. Kiryat Shmona, on the other hand, recorded its fifth defeat in a row. The three points were Netanya's first since the start of the run.

It was also the first game since the opening round of the season in which Netanya did not concede a goal. The team praised goalkeeper Samuel Silva and defender Olivier Verdon, as well as Romanian midfielder Gabriel Simion, who started for the first time since signing. Midfielder Dolev Haziza was not included in the squad because of renewed pain in a leg that was injured in the past.

In Netanya they described the win as an event that released much of the pressure on the team, and compared it to the splitting of the Red Sea. The win came in a week in which the team was under pressure to get results, after going four rounds without a win.
Netanya's next game is away against Ironi Tiberias, who are in last place in the table. Another win there would be the first time this season that Maccabi Netanya wins two games in a row.
keyPoints: 1-0 win over Ironi Kiryat Shmona, from a second-half penalty
End of a run of four games without a win
Maccabi Netanya moved up to sixth place, at least temporarily
maccabi-netanya-beat-kiryat-shmona.whatItMeans: Maccabi Netanya fans got a win that returns the team to the upper part of the table before the away game in Tiberias.
faq: Who scored the goal?
Matheus Dabo, from a penalty kick taken from 11 meters, around the 74th minute.
Where is Maccabi Netanya in the table after the win?
In sixth place, at least temporarily.

netanya-five-urban-renewal-plans.title: Five pinui-binui (demolish and rebuild) plans in Netanya head for deposit, with about 1,300 new apartments
netanya-five-urban-renewal-plans.dek: The subcommittee for planning and building decided to deposit, with conditions, five plans in the city center, Kiryat Nordau and Neot Shaked, which will replace hundreds of old apartments.
body: In early September, the subcommittee of the local planning and building committee in Netanya decided to deposit (publish for public review and objections) five urban renewal plans, subject to conditions. Together they include about 1,300 new apartments, in place of hundreds of older apartments that will be demolished.

In the city center, in the Dizengoff and Shtemfer compound, about 300 apartments are planned in place of 102, in two towers of 20 to 35 floors on a shared four-floor base, and one building in the compound will be preserved. In Kiryat Nordau, in the Shitrit compound, 84 apartments will be replaced by 320 new apartments, in four buildings of 10, 27 and 30 floors, with a commercial frontage and public spaces.

In the Neot Shaked neighborhood, two towers of 30 and 35 floors with 315 apartments are planned, in place of 80 apartments in two railway-style apartment blocks (binyanei rakevet). The height of the towers is subject to approval by the Civil Aviation Authority. On Binyamin Boulevard and Brodetsky Street, a 31-floor tower and two 17-floor buildings will be built, with 240 apartments in place of 75, as well as a public parking lot with fees.

The fifth plan is the Sharon Cinema compound in the city center, near Smilansky and Sha'ar HaGai streets. In place of about 62 apartments, a mixed-use tower of 35 floors with 130 apartments will be built, and the cinema building will be preserved for cultural, commercial and employment uses.

The head of the municipality's Urban Renewal Administration said that urban renewal is not only the replacement of old buildings with new ones. Mayor Avi Salama said it is an opportunity to renew the older neighborhoods and improve residents' lives.
keyPoints: Five plans approved for deposit, with conditions, in early September
About 1,300 new apartments in the city center, Kiryat Nordau and Neot Shaked
The Sharon Cinema building will be preserved for cultural and commercial uses
netanya-five-urban-renewal-plans.whatItMeans: Residents in these compounds and nearby can review the plans and file objections during the deposit period, once it is announced.
faq: What does a decision to deposit a plan mean?
The plan is published to the public, and objections can be filed against it before a final decision is made.
In which neighborhoods are the plans located?
Three in the city center, one in Kiryat Nordau and one in Neot Shaked.

netanya-hamitmad-bialik-tower.title: Renewal plan near Independence Square in Netanya deposited: 114 apartments instead of 49
netanya-hamitmad-bialik-tower.dek: The plan on HaMitmad and Bialik streets includes a 27-floor tower, and objections can now be filed against it.
body: An urban renewal plan at 3 to 5 HaMitmad Street and 8 Bialik Street, near Independence Square in central Netanya, has moved to the deposit stage. At this stage, the plan documents can be reviewed and objections can be filed under the Planning and Building Law. The plan covers about 3.1 dunams (a dunam is 1,000 square meters), and its number is 408-1098342. The report did not give the developer's name.

Today the compound has three older buildings with 49 apartments. On HaMitmad Street there are two three-floor buildings with 28 apartments, which are slated for demolition. In their place a residential tower of 27 floors with 91 apartments will be built.

The building at 8 Bialik Street, which has 21 apartments, will not be demolished. It will be strengthened and expanded, and will include 23 apartments on about eight floors. In total there will be 114 apartments in the compound, an addition of 65 apartments.
On the ground floor of the tower, a built public space is planned, which will be registered in the name of the Netanya Municipality. Its use has not yet been determined.

The local planning and building committee approved the plan for deposit in May 2026. According to the planning databases, its status was updated on October 13, and the deposit notice was updated later that same week. It is important to know that a deposit is not a building permit. No date has yet been published for demolition or the start of construction, and the plan still has to go through a hearing on objections and final approval. During the deposit period, anyone who considers themselves harmed by the plan may file an objection.
keyPoints: A 27-floor tower on HaMitmad Street in place of two older buildings
The building at 8 Bialik Street will be strengthened and expanded to 23 apartments
The plan is at the objections stage and is not a building permit
netanya-hamitmad-bialik-tower.whatItMeans: Neighbors and property owners near Independence Square can now review the plan and file an objection if they believe it harms them.
faq: Can construction start now?
No. A deposit is not a building permit, and the plan still needs a hearing on objections and final approval.
How many apartments will be in the compound?
114 apartments, instead of 49 today.

dora-renewal-no-area-cap.title: Dora compound: municipality backs away from capping the added area of the new apartments
dora-renewal-no-area-cap.dek: After a lengthy legal process, the district appeals committee determined that the addition to apartments in the renewal project in southern Netanya will not be capped.
body: The Netanya Municipality gave up its demand to cap the addition to the new apartments in the Dora compound, in Ramat Yadin in the south of the city. As a result, the Central District Planning and Building Appeals Committee determined that the addition will not be capped.

The plan in the compound replaces 88 old apartments in railway-style apartment blocks (binyanei rakevet) with 320 new apartments. The local committee approved it in January 2025, but made the approval conditional on each new apartment being larger than the old one by no more than 12 sq m, plus a balcony. The condition relied on a municipal policy document from 2019.

The residents appealed. In December 2025 the appeals committee rejected their request for permission to appeal, and they petitioned the Central District Court in Lod. In July the court accepted the petition and returned the matter to the district committee. The municipality reconsidered its position and announced that the 2019 policy does not apply to the plan, because the compound was first discussed in 2013 and was declared a pinui-binui (demolish and rebuild) compound that same year by a government decision. The parties filed an agreed notice, and the proceeding ended.

According to the residents' contracts with the developers, each new apartment will be at least 85 sq m, or the size of the old apartment plus 20 sq m, whichever is larger. Most of the old apartments are about 46 sq m, so some residents may receive an addition of up to about 40 sq m.
The municipality stated that this is a plan from 2013 and that the current compensation policy does not apply to it.
keyPoints: In the Dora project, 320 new apartments will replace 88 old ones
The municipality announced that its 2019 policy of a 12 sq m cap does not apply to the plan
A new apartment will be at least 85 sq m, or the old one plus 20 sq m
dora-renewal-no-area-cap.whatItMeans: Residents of the Dora compound will receive larger apartments according to what was agreed with the developers, but the decision concerns this plan and does not change the policy in the rest of the city.
faq: Does the decision apply to all renewal projects in Netanya?
No. According to the municipality, the policy does not apply to Dora because the plan was first discussed in 2013, before the policy was approved.
How many apartments will be built in the compound?
320 new apartments in place of 88 old ones.

nordau-max-betterment-levy-appeal.title: Appeals committee: betterment levy in the Nordau Max project expected to fall by tens of millions of shekels
nordau-max-betterment-levy-appeal.dek: The arbitrating appraiser estimated the levy at about NIS 10.45 million, much less than the municipality's original demand, and the final decision is still open.
body: The Central District Appeals Committee for Compensation and Betterment Levies discussed an assessment by an arbitrating appraiser on the “Nordau Max” project in Kiryat Nordau, in a dispute between the developer, the Damri company, and the local planning and building committee in Netanya.

In the project, near Route 2, seven old railway-style apartment blocks (binyanei rakevet) with 138 apartments will be demolished, and in their place three residential towers with commercial space will be built, with a total of 553 apartments. The plan came into effect in September 2022.

The economic feasibility study carried out for the plan estimated the betterment levy (heitel hashbacha, a payment to the local authority on the rise in land value due to a plan) at about NIS 9 million. By contrast, the municipality's original assessment demanded about NIS 93 million. During the appeal, the municipality reduced its demand to about NIS 41.6 million, and the developer argued that the plan creates no betterment at all. The arbitrating appraiser estimated the betterment at about NIS 20.9 million, meaning a levy of about NIS 10.45 million.

One of the central questions was whether a levy should be charged on building rights intended for safe rooms (mamad). The committee adopted the alternative that exempts these rights. It determined that the feasibility study's estimate does not bind the authority, but when there is a large gap between it and the later assessment, a convincing professional explanation is required, and the municipality's explanation did not meet that standard.

The appraiser will carry out further checks, among them whether rights under Tama 38 (the national plan for strengthening buildings against earthquakes) can be realized. Both sides appealed the assessment, so the amount of the final levy has not yet been determined.
keyPoints: The municipality initially demanded about NIS 93 million in betterment levy
The arbitrating appraiser estimated the levy at about NIS 10.45 million
Both sides appealed, and the final levy is still open
nordau-max-betterment-levy-appeal.whatItMeans: The decision may affect how the municipality calculates betterment levies in urban renewal projects, especially regarding rights for safe rooms.
faq: What is a betterment levy (heitel hashbacha)?

A payment to the local authority on the rise in the value of real estate following the approval of a plan. Here it was determined in a process involving an arbitrating appraiser and an appeals committee.
Has the final amount already been determined?
No. The appraiser still has to complete further checks, and both sides appealed the assessment.

netanya-culture-hall-late-october.title: At the Netanya Culture Hall in the next two weeks: a new Israeli play, music shows and children's shows
netanya-culture-hall-late-october.dek: The Culture Hall's program includes an evening about Toledo, the new play “HaMoradot,” and family shows in early November.
body: The Netanya Culture Hall (Heichal HaTarbut) is announcing a series of shows for the coming weeks. Most of the events take place in the Auditorium hall, and some are also available as part of a subscription. On Monday, October 26, at 20:30, the “Fascinating Cities” series will open with an evening about Toledo called “Viva Espana.”

On Thursday, October 29, at 20:30, “HaMoradot,” a new Israeli play by Amnon Levy, will be staged, and additional dates are planned for the show. On Tuesday, November 3, at 20:30, Miri Chen will host Moshe Lahav in the show “Songs from the Movies,” as part of the “Israeli Celebration” series.

For families: on Wednesday, November 4, at 17:30, “Aladdin,” a new show for the whole family, will be staged. On Monday, November 9, at 17:30, the show “Autumn in All Colors, the Magic of Color” will be staged. On Monday, November 16, at 17:30, the show “Miki, Yael's House” will be staged. For senior citizens: on Tuesday, November 17, at 09:00, the peak event of Senior Citizens Month will take place, “Hakol Over Chabibi” (“Everything Passes, Habibi”) with Anabella Shaked.

For adults: on Saturday night, November 7 (after Shabbat), at 21:00, “Charlie and a Half” will be staged. On Monday, November 9, at 11:00, the musical show “La Dolce Vita” with Orit Gabrieli will take place as part of “Cultural Monday.” On Thursday, November 12, at 20:00, an evening marking Aliyah Day will be held, and on Saturday night, November 14, at 21:00, Yuval Semo will perform.
Tickets and more details are available on the Culture Hall's ticketing website. It is worth checking the dates before you arrive, because the schedule of shows is updated from time to time.
keyPoints: “HaMoradot,” a new play by Amnon Levy, on October 29
Miri Chen hosts Moshe Lahav on November 3
Family shows on November 4 and 9
netanya-culture-hall-late-october.whatItMeans: Residents of Netanya can find shows for adults and children in the next two weeks without leaving the city.
faq: Where are the shows held?
In the Auditorium hall of the Netanya Culture Hall.
How do I buy tickets?
On the ticketing website of the Netanya Culture Hall, and some of the shows are also available through a subscription.

netanya-beach-race-december-2026.title: Netanya Beach Race returns: Friday, December 4, with start and finish at Poleg Beach
netanya-beach-race-december-2026.dek: The race combines road running and sand running, and will include 10 km and 5 km heats alongside community runs for children and families.
body: The Netanya Beach Race will be held again this year, on Friday, December 4. The race is organized by the Netanya Municipality and its sports department, and produced by the Shvoong company. The start and finish area will be at Poleg Beach, one of the city's nine declared bathing beaches.

The main event is a competitive 10 km run that combines a fast road section with a run on the seashore. Alongside it there will be a competitive 5 km heat along the road and the beach, which also suits those looking for a more accessible route, and includes a section inside a nature reserve.

For children, teenagers and families there will be community runs of 2 km and 1.2 km, so that even someone who does not run regularly can take part. The different routes allow participation at every level, from competitive runners to families with children.

The route passes through some of the city's most beautiful spots and along the coastline, combining urban road running with running on sand. In the finish area at Poleg Beach there will be a sports and healthy lifestyle fair, with music and food stands, and all finishers will receive a medal.

Registration opened with the announcement in August, at early-registration prices for a limited time, through a registration link of the production company. Current prices and dates should be checked on the race's registration page before registering. When the announcement was published, the early-registration period was set at only ten days.
keyPoints: Friday, December 4, start and finish at Poleg Beach
10 km and 5 km heats, plus community runs
A medal for every finisher and a sports fair on the beach
netanya-beach-race-december-2026.whatItMeans: Runners and families from Netanya and the Sharon can register for an urban seaside sports event at the start of winter.
faq: Where does the race start?
The start and finish area are at Poleg Beach.
Are there heats for children?
Yes, community runs of 2 km and 1.2 km for children, teenagers and families.

emek-hefer-swim-aquathlon-2026.title: Emek Hefer swim and aquathlon to take place on November 21 at the Beit Yanai beaches
emek-hefer-swim-aquathlon-2026.dek: The event includes swims from 600 meters to 4.7 km and aquathlon heats for adults and children, at the beaches of Beit Yanai National Park.
body: The Emek Hefer Swim 2026 will be held on Saturday, November 21, at the beaches of Beit Yanai National Park on the Emek Hefer coast, north of Netanya. Alongside the swim there will also be an aquathlon, a competition that combines swimming and running. The organizers present the event as a sea festival on a white-sand beach.

The swim will have three competitive heats, of 4.7 km, 2.5 km and 1.2 km, as well as a community swim of 600 meters, which also suits those who are not competitive swimmers. The website also lists the shortest heat as a 1 km heat, so it is worth confirming the exact length with the organizers.

In the adult aquathlon, participants will swim 750 meters and then run. The event website gives two different figures for the length of the run, so it is worth checking the final route with the organizers. In the children's aquathlon, the swim is 500 meters and the run is 1.7 km.

The event is produced by Shvoong, a company that produces sports events. According to the website, about 700 athletes took part in last year's event, and the website also has the 2025 results, a photo album and a score table for the swim league.

Registration is done through the event website. Prices are published on a separate page, and the start times and the registration closing date were not detailed on the main page, so it is recommended to check them on the website before registering. The 600-meter community swim is intended for the general public and not only for competitive swimmers.
keyPoints: Saturday, November 21, at the beaches of Beit Yanai National Park
Swims of 600 meters, 1.2, 2.5 and 4.7 km
Aquathlon for adults and children
emek-hefer-swim-aquathlon-2026.whatItMeans: Swimmers and runners from Netanya and the Sharon can take part in a sea competition close to home, a short drive from the city.
faq: When and where will the swim be held?
On Saturday, November 21, at the beaches of Beit Yanai National Park in Emek Hefer.
Is there a heat for children?
Yes, an aquathlon for children with a 500-meter swim and a 1.7 km run.

kfar-yona-october-updates.title: Kfar Yona: 94% bagrut eligibility, a new business community and programming courses for teenagers
kfar-yona-october-updates.dek: The Kfar Yona Municipality published a series of updates for residents in October, from education data to guidelines ahead of the Knesset elections.
body: The Kfar Yona Municipality published a series of updates for residents on its website during October. The latest update, from October 22, reports 94% bagrut (matriculation) eligibility in the city and IDF enlistment rates that are among the highest in the country. The updates appear on the home page of the municipality's website, by publication date.

On October 20, the municipality announced new courses in programming and artificial intelligence for teenagers. The same day it also published the launch of “Beit Mechubarot,” together with a stand-up show by Yona Kapach to be held on November 1.

On October 11, the municipality announced the establishment of the Kfar Yona business community, which is getting under way. Earlier, on October 6, the municipality published a call for residents to join the city's mediators team. At the end of September it also published the “Inspiring Meetings” initiative, one hour a week of a meeting with seniors (the third age), and in mid-September a survey on employment services.

Ahead of the Knesset elections, to be held on Tuesday, October 27, the municipality published on October 8 the procedure for hanging election campaign posters in the city. Anyone planning to hang posters must act according to the published procedure.

The full details of each of the updates, including how to register for the courses and for the mediators team, are published in the news section of the municipality's website. Residents can also contact the municipality by phone at *6769, which is listed on the website. The website also has the municipality's full news archive.
keyPoints: 94% bagrut eligibility in Kfar Yona, according to the municipality's update
New programming and artificial intelligence courses for teenagers
A local business community and an initiative to recruit mediators
kfar-yona-october-updates.whatItMeans: Residents of Kfar Yona are invited to join new initiatives, and teenagers can register for technology courses through the municipality.
faq: When is Yona Kapach's stand-up show in Kfar Yona?
On November 1, as part of the launch of “Beit Mechubarot.”
How do I contact the Kfar Yona Municipality?
Through the municipality's website or by phone at *6769.
